items.title: bad to finish polishing car outside if it's cloudy?
items.text:
bad to finish polishing car outside if it's cloudy?
there is no direct sunlight with it being cloudy, as i have read in some places that polishing in direct sunlight can make things significantly more difficult.

&#x200B;

i can't find much on the cloudy conditions though. thanks for the tips if any
Neat thanks :D I'm so excited.. been a lurker for years, saw a sale and splurged on loads of detailing stuff.. thanks for the help :)
Thanks :)

hey! :D

yeah! i got a harbor freight DA polisher, used meguiars 205/105 combo, and some yellow wax. did a de-iron, bug tar, clayed, the whole nine ... lol

my tc looks better than when i got it!

what i have found as a complete newbie:

if your paint was like mine - 2yrs old, 34k/mi, and NEVER did a touch wash (manual power wash, or no touch), and mostly have normal road wear and rock chips to high hell (i did mostly highway to work), 205 with a polish pad will remove .... 70%? or scratches and almost 95% of swirls.. the 105 compound is serious stuff..

it will be expensive to have, but if you do a 3x3 square in a inconspicuous spot on your car like the guides say, you can see if your really need to go straight 105 or do a 205/105 mixture. [WATCH THIS](https://youtu.be/4ocjnIiZMQ8?t=448). i time stamped exactly what i just said. I tried it and felt good with only doing a 205 polish.

A LOT of people apparently do 205/105 mixed cause to need a 3 step polish would be insane..

im not a pro, or amateur even ^^LOL, but this is what i've gathered from lurking and watching hundreds of videos and reviews lmao
